verses.1: The vision which Isaiah, son of Amoz, had concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
verses.2: Hear, O heavens, and listen, O earth, for the LORD speaks: Sons have I raised and reared, but they have disowned me!
verses.3: An ox knows its owner, and an ass, its master's manger; But Israel does not know, my people has not understood.
verses.4: Ah! sinful nation, people laden with wickedness, evil race, corrupt children! They have forsaken the LORD, spurned the Holy One of Israel, apostatized.
verses.5: Where would you yet be struck, you that rebel again and again? The whole head is sick, the whole heart faint.
verses.6: From the sole of the foot to the head there is no sound spot: Wound and welt and gaping gash, not drained, or bandaged, or eased with salve.
verses.7: Your country is waste, your cities burnt with fire; Your land before your eyes strangers devour (a waste, like Sodom overthrown) -
verses.8: And daughter Zion is left like a hut in a vineyard, Like a shed in a melon patch, like a city blockaded.
verses.9: Unless the LORD of hosts had left us a scanty remnant, We had become as Sodom, we should be like Gomorrah.
verses.10: Hear the word of the LORD, princes of Sodom! Listen to the instruction of our God, people of Gomorrah!
verses.11: What care I for the number of your sacrifices? says the LORD. I have had enough of whole-burnt rams and fat of fatlings; In the blood of calves, lambs and goats I find no pleasure.
verses.12: When you come in to visit me, who asks these things of you?
verses.13: Trample my courts no more! Bring no more worthless offerings; your incense is loathsome to me. New moon and sabbath, calling of assemblies, octaves with wickedness: these I cannot bear.
verses.14: Your new moons and festivals I detest; they weigh me down, I tire of the load.
verses.15: When you spread out your hands, I close my eyes to you; Though you pray the more, I will not listen. Your hands are full of blood!
verses.16: Wash yourselves clean! Put away your misdeeds from before my eyes; cease doing evil;
verses.17: learn to do good. Make justice your aim: redress the wronged, hear the orphan's plea, defend the widow.
verses.18: Come now, let us set things right, says the LORD: Though your sins be like scarlet, they may become white as snow; Though they be crimson red, they may become white as wool.
verses.19: If you are willing, and obey, you shall eat the good things of the land;
verses.20: But if you refuse and resist, the sword shall consume you: for the mouth of the LORD has spoken!
verses.21: How has she turned adulteress, the faithful city, so upright! Justice used to lodge within her, but now, murderers.
verses.22: Your silver is turned to dross, your wine is mixed with water.
verses.23: Your princes are rebels and comrades of thieves; Each one of them loves a bribe and looks for gifts. The fatherless they defend not, and the widow's plea does not reach them.
verses.24: Now, therefore, says the Lord, the LORD of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: Ah! I will take vengeance on my foes and fully repay my enemies!
verses.25: I will turn my hand against you, and refine your dross in the furnace, removing all your alloy.
verses.26: I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as in the beginning; After that you shall be called city of justice, faithful city.
verses.27: Zion shall be redeemed by judgment, and her repentant ones by justice.
verses.28: Rebels and sinners alike shall be crushed, those who desert the LORD shall be consumed.
verses.29: You shall be ashamed of the terebinths which you prized, and blush for the groves which you chose.
verses.30: You shall become like a tree with falling leaves, like a garden that has no water.
verses.31: The strong man shall turn to tow, and his work shall become a spark; Both shall burn together, and there shall be none to quench the flames.
verses.32: This is what Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.33: In days to come, The mountain of the LORD'S house shall be established as the highest mountain and raised above the hills. All nations shall stream toward it;
verses.34: many peoples shall come and say: "Come, let us climb the LORD'S mountain, to the house of the God of Jacob, That he may instruct us in his ways, and we may walk in his paths." For from Zion shall go forth instruction, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
verses.35: He shall judge between the nations, and impose terms on many peoples. They shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; One nation shall not raise the sword against another, nor shall they train for war again.
verses.36: O house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the LORD!
verses.37: You have abandoned your people, the house of Jacob, Because they are filled with fortunetellers and soothsayers, like the Philistines; they covenant with strangers.
verses.38: Their land is full of silver and gold, and there is no end to their treasures; Their land is full of horses, and there is no end to their chariots.
verses.39: Their land is full of idols; they worship the works of their hands, that which their fingers have made.
verses.40: But man is abased, each one brought low. (Do not pardon them!
verses.41: Get behind the rocks, hide in the dust, From the terror of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty!
verses.42: The haughty eyes of man will be lowered, the arrogance of men will be abased, and the LORD alone will be exalted, on that day.
verses.43: For the LORD of hosts will have his day against all that is proud and arrogant, all that is high, and it will be brought low;
verses.44: Yes, against all the cedars of Lebanon and all the oaks of Bashan,
verses.45: Against all the lofty mountains and all the high hills,
verses.46: Against every lofty tower and every fortified wall,
verses.47: Against all the ships of Tarshish and all stately vessels.
verses.48: Human pride will be abased, the arrogance of men brought low, And the LORD alone will be exalted, on that day.
verses.50: Men will go into caves in the rocks and into holes in the earth, From the terror of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty, when he arises to overawe the earth.
verses.51: On that day men will throw to the moles and the bats the idols of silver and gold which they made for worship.
verses.52: They go into caverns in the rocks and into crevices in the cliffs, From the terror of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty, when he arises to overawe the earth.
verses.53: As for you, let man alone, in whose nostrils is but a breath; for what is he worth?
verses.54: The Lord, the LORD of hosts, shall take away from Jerusalem and from Judah support and prop (all supplies of bread and water):
verses.55: Hero and warrior, judge and prophet, fortune-teller and elder,
verses.56: The captain of fifty and the nobleman, counselor, skilled magician, and expert charmer.
verses.57: I will make striplings their princes; the fickle shall govern them,
verses.58: And the people shall oppress one another, yes, every man his neighbor. The child shall be bold toward the elder, and the base toward the honorable.
verses.59: When a man seizes his brother in his father's house, saying, "You have clothes! Be our ruler, and take in hand this ruin!" -
verses.60: Then shall he answer in that day: "I will not undertake to cure this, when in my own house there is no bread or clothing! You shall not make me ruler of the people."
verses.61: Jerusalem is crumbling, Judah is falling; for their speech and their deeds are before the LORD, a provocation in the sight of his majesty.
verses.62: Their very look bears witness against them; their sin like Sodom they vaunt, They hide it not. Woe to them! they deal out evil to themselves.
verses.63: Happy the just, for it will be well with them, the fruit of their works they will eat.
verses.64: Woe to the wicked man! All goes ill, with the work of his hands he will be repaid.
verses.65: My people - a babe in arms will be their tyrant, and women will rule them! O my people, your leaders mislead, they destroy the paths you should follow.
verses.66: The LORD rises to accuse, standing to try his people.
verses.67: The Lord enters into judgment with his people's elders and princes: It is you who have devoured the vineyard; the loot wrested from the poor is in your houses.
verses.68: What do you mean by crushing my people, and grinding down the poor when they look to you? says the Lord, the GOD of hosts.
verses.69: The LORD said: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with necks outstretched Ogling and mincing as they go, their anklets tinkling with every step,
verses.70: The Lord shall cover the scalps of Zion's daughters with scabs, and the LORD shall bare their heads.
verses.71: On that day the LORD will do away with the finery of the anklets, sunbursts, and crescents;
verses.73: the headdresses, bangles, cinctures, perfume boxes, and amulets;
verses.74: the signet rings, and the nose rings;
verses.75: the court dresses, wraps, cloaks, and purses;
verses.76: the mirrors, linen tunics, turbans, and shawls.
verses.77: Instead of perfume there will be stench, instead of the girdle, a rope, And for the coiffure, baldness; for the rich gown, a sackcloth skirt. Then, instead of beauty:
verses.78: Your men will fall by the sword, and your champions, in war;
verses.79: Her gates will lament and mourn, as the city sits desolate on the ground.
verses.80: Seven women will take hold of one man on that day, saying: "We will eat our own food and wear our own clothing; Only let your name be given us, put an end to our disgrace!"
verses.81: On that day, The branch of the LORD will be luster and glory, and the fruit of the earth will be honor and splendor for the survivors of Israel.
verses.82: He who remains in Zion and he that is left in Jerusalem Will be called holy: every one marked down for life in Jerusalem.
verses.83: When the Lord washes away the filth of the daughters of Zion, And purges Jerusalem's blood from her midst with a blast of searing judgment,
verses.84: Then will the LORD create, over the whole site of Mount Zion and over her place of assembly, A smoking cloud by day and a light of flaming fire by night.
verses.85: For over all, his glory will be shelter and protection: shade from the parching heat of day, refuge and cover from storm and rain.
verses.116: 2 In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a high and lofty throne, with the train of his garment filling the temple.
verses.117: Seraphim were stationed above; each of them had six wings: with two they veiled their faces, with two they veiled their feet, and with two they hovered aloft.
verses.118: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts!" they cried one to the other. "All the earth is filled with his glory!"
verses.119: At the sound of that cry, the frame of the door shook and the house was filled with smoke.
verses.120: Then I said, "Woe is me, I am doomed! For I am a man of unclean lips, living among a people of unclean lips; yet my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts!"
verses.121: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, holding an ember which he had taken with tongs from the altar.
verses.122: He touched my mouth with it. "See," he said, "now that this has touched your lips, your wickedness is removed, your sin purged."
verses.123: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send? Who will go for us?" "Here I am," I said; "send me!"
verses.124: And he replied: Go and say to this people: Listen carefully, but you shall not understand! Look intently, but you shall know nothing!
verses.125: You are to make the heart of this people sluggish, to dull their ears and close their eyes; Else their eyes will see, their ears hear, their heart understand, and they will turn and be healed.
verses.126: "How long, O Lord?" I asked. And he replied: Until the cities are desolate, without inhabitants, Houses, without a man, and the earth is a desolate waste.
verses.127: Until the LORD removes men far away, and the land is abandoned more and more.
verses.128: If there be still a tenth part in it, then this in turn shall be laid waste; As with a terebinth or an oak whose trunk remains when its leaves have fallen. (Holy offspring is the trunk.
verses.129: In the days of Ahaz, king of Judah, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah, king of Israel, son of Remaliah, went up to attack Jerusalem, but they were not able to conquer it.
verses.130: When word came to the house of David that Aram was encamped in Ephraim, the heart of the king and heart of the people trembled, as the trees of the forest tremble in the wind.
verses.131: Then the LORD said to Isaiah: Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway of the fuller's field,
verses.132: and say to him: Take care you remain tranquil and do not fear; let not your courage fail before these two stumps of smoldering brands (the blazing anger of Rezin and the Arameans, and of the son of Remaliah),
verses.133: because of the mischief that Aram (Ephraim and the son of Remaliah) plots against you, saying,
verses.134: "Let us go up and tear Judah asunder, make it our own by force, and appoint the son of Tabeel king there."
verses.135: Thus says the LORD: This shall not stand, it shall not be!
verses.136: Damascus is the capital of Aram, and Rezin the head of Damascus; Samaria is the capital of Ephraim, and Remaliah's son the head of Samaria.
verses.137: But within sixty years and five, Ephraim shall be crushed, no longer a nation. Unless your faith is firm you shall not be firm!
verses.138: Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz:
verses.139: Ask for a sign from the LORD, your God; let it be deep as the nether world, or high as the sky!
verses.140: But Ahaz answered, "I will not ask! I will not tempt the LORD!"
verses.141: Then he said: Listen, O house of David! Is it not enough for you to weary men, must you also weary my God?
verses.142: Therefore the Lord himself will give you this sign: the virgin shall be with child, and bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
verses.143: He shall be living on curds and honey by the time he learns to reject the bad and choose the good.
verses.144: For before the child learns to reject the bad and choose the good, the land of those two kings whom you dread shall be deserted.
verses.145: The LORD shall bring upon you and your people and your father's house days worse than any since Ephraim seceded from Judah. (This means the king of Assyria.
verses.146: On that day The LORD shall whistle for the fly that is in the farthest streams of Egypt, and for the bee in the land of Assyria.
verses.147: All of them shall come and settle in the steep ravines and in the rocky clefts, on all thornbushes and in all pastures.
verses.148: On that day the LORD shall shave with the razor hired from across the River (with the king of Assyria) the head, and the hair between the legs. It shall also shave off the beard.
verses.149: On that day a man shall keep a heifer or a couple of sheep,
verses.150: and from their abundant yield of milk he shall live on curds; curds and honey shall be the food of all who remain in the land.
verses.151: On that day every place where there used to be a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, shall be turned to briers and thorns.
verses.152: Men shall go there with bow and arrows; for all the country shall be briers and thorns.
verses.153: For fear of briers and thorns you shall not go upon any mountainside which used to be hoed with the mattock; they shall be grazing land for cattle and shall be trampled upon by sheep.
verses.197: Woe to those who enact unjust statutes and who write oppressive decrees,
verses.198: Depriving the needy of judgment and robbing my people's poor of their rights, Making widows their plunder, and orphans their prey!
verses.199: What will you do on the day of punishment, when ruin comes from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth,
verses.200: Lest it sink beneath the captive or fall beneath the slain? For all this, his wrath is not turned back, his hand is still outstretched!
verses.201: Woe to Assyria! My rod in anger, my staff in wrath.
verses.202: Against an impious nation I send him, and against a people under my wrath I order him To seize plunder, carry off loot, and tread them down like the mud of the streets.
verses.203: But this is not what he intends, nor does he have this in mind; Rather, it is in his heart to destroy, to make an end of nations not a few.
verses.204: "Are not my commanders all kings?" he says,
verses.205: "Is not Calno like Carchemish, Or Hamath like Arpad, or Samaria like Damascus?
verses.206: Just as my hand reached out to idolatrous kingdoms that had more images than Jerusalem and Samaria,
verses.207: Just as I treated Samaria and her idols, shall I not do to Jerusalem and her graven images?"
verses.208: (But when the LORD has brought to an end all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I will punish the utterance of the king of Assyria's proud heart,
verses.209: and the boastfulness of his haughty eyes. For he says:) "By my own power I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I am shrewd. I have moved the boundaries of peoples, their treasures I have pillaged, and, like a giant, I have put down the enthroned.
verses.210: My hand has seized like a nest the riches of nations; As one takes eggs left alone, so I took in all the earth; No one fluttered a wing, or opened a mouth, or chirped!"
verses.211: Will the axe boast against him who hews with it? Will the saw exalt itself above him who wields it? As if a rod could sway him who lifts it, or a staff him who is not wood!
verses.212: Therefore the Lord, the LORD of hosts, will send among his fat ones leanness, And instead of his glory there will be kindling like the kindling of fire.
verses.213: The Light of Israel will become a fire, Israel's Holy One a flame, That burns and consumes his briers and his thorns in a single day.
verses.214: His splendid forests and orchards will be consumed, soul and body;
verses.215: And the remnant of the trees in his forest will be so few, Like poles set up for signals, that any boy can record them.
verses.216: On that day The remnant of Israel, the survivors of the house of Jacob, will no more lean upon him who struck them; But they lean upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
verses.217: A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.
verses.218: For though your people, O Israel, were like the sand of the sea, Only a remnant of them will return; their destruction is decreed as overwhelming justice demands.
verses.219: Yes, the destruction he has decreed, the Lord, the GOD of hosts, will carry out within the whole land.
verses.220: Therefore thus says the Lord, the GOD of hosts: O my people, who dwell in Zion, do not fear the Assyrian, though he strikes you with a rod, and raises his staff against you.
verses.221: For only a brief moment more, and my anger shall be over; but them I will destroy in wrath.
verses.222: Then the LORD of hosts will raise against them a scourge such as struck Midian at the rock of Oreb; and he will raise his staff over the sea as he did against Egypt.
verses.223: On that day, His burden shall be taken from your shoulder, and his yoke shattered from your neck. He has come up from the direction of Rimmon,
verses.224: he has reached Aiath, passed through Migron, at Michmash his supplies are stored.
verses.225: They cross the ravine: "We will spend the night at Geba." Ramah is in terror, Gibeah of Saul has fled.
verses.226: Cry and shriek, O daughter of Gallim! Hearken, Laishah! Answer her, Anathoth!
verses.227: Madmenah is in flight, the inhabitants of Gebim seek refuge.
verses.228: Even today he will halt at Nob, he will shake his fist at the mount of daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem!
verses.229: Behold, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, lops off the boughs with terrible violence; The tall of stature are felled, and the lofty ones brought low;
verses.230: The forest thickets are felled with the axe, and Lebanon in its splendor falls.
verses.231: But a shoot shall sprout from the stump of Jesse, and from his roots a bud shall blossom.
verses.232: The spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him: a spirit of wisdom and of understanding, A spirit of counsel and of strength, a spirit of knowledge and of fear of the LORD,
verses.233: and his delight shall be the fear of the LORD. Not by appearance shall he judge, nor by hearsay shall he decide,
verses.234: But he shall judge the poor with justice, and decide aright for the land's afflicted. He shall strike the ruthless with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked.
verses.235: Justice shall be the band around his waist, and faithfulness a belt upon his hips.
verses.236: Then the wolf shall be a guest of the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; The calf and the young lion shall browse together, with a little child to guide them.
verses.237: The cow and the bear shall be neighbors, together their young shall rest; the lion shall eat hay like the ox.
verses.238: The baby shall play by the cobra's den, and the child lay his hand on the adder's lair.
verses.239: There shall be no harm or ruin on all my holy mountain; for the earth shall be filled with knowledge of the LORD, as water covers the sea.
verses.240: On that day, The root of Jesse, set up as a signal for the nations, The Gentiles shall seek out, for his dwelling shall be glorious.
verses.241: On that day, The Lord shall again take it in hand to reclaim the remnant of his people that is left from Assyria and Egypt, Pathros, Ethiopia, and Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the isles of the sea.
verses.242: He shall raise a signal to the nations and gather the outcasts of Israel; The dispersed of Judah he shall assemble from the four corners of the earth.
verses.243: The envy of Ephraim shall pass away, and the rivalry of Judah be removed; Ephraim shall not be jealous of Judah, and Judah shall not be hostile to Ephraim;
verses.244: But they shall swoop down on the foothills of the Philistines to the west, together they shall plunder the Kedemites; Edom and Moab shall be their possessions, and the Ammonites their subjects.
verses.245: The LORD shall dry up the tongue of the Sea of Egypt, and wave his hand over the Euphrates in his fierce anger And shatter it into seven streamlets, so that it can be crossed in sandals.
verses.246: There shall be a highway for the remnant of his people that is left from Assyria, As there was for Israel when he came up from the land of Egypt.
verses.247: On that day, you will say: I give you thanks, O LORD; though you have been angry with me, your anger has abated, and you have consoled me.
verses.248: God indeed is my savior; I am confident and unafraid. My strength and my courage is the LORD, and he has been my savior.
verses.249: With joy you will draw water at the fountain of salvation,
verses.250: and say on that day: Give thanks to the LORD, acclaim his name; among the nations make known his deeds, proclaim how exalted is his name.
verses.251: Sing praise to the LORD for his glorious achievement; let this be known throughout all the earth.
verses.252: Shout with exultation, O city of Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel!
verses.253: An oracle concerning Babylon; a vision of Isaiah, son of Amoz.
verses.254: Upon the bare mountains set up a signal; cry out to them, Wave for them to enter the gates of the volunteers.
verses.255: I have commanded my dedicated soldiers, I have summoned my warriors, eager and bold to carry out my anger.
verses.256: Listen! the rumble on the mountains: that of an immense throng! Listen! the noise of kingdoms, nations assembled! The LORD of hosts is mustering an army for battle.
verses.257: They come from a far-off country, and from the end of the heavens, The LORD and the instruments of his wrath, to destroy all the land.
verses.258: Howl, for the day of the LORD is near; as destruction from the Almighty it comes.
verses.259: Therefore all hands fall helpless, the bows of the young men fall from their hands. Every man's heart melts
verses.260: in terror. Pangs and sorrows take hold of them, like a woman in labor they writhe; They look aghast at each other, their faces aflame.
verses.261: Lo, the day of the LORD comes, cruel, with wrath and burning anger; To lay waste the land and destroy the sinners within it!
verses.262: The stars and constellations of the heavens send forth no light; The sun is dark when it rises, and the light of the moon does not shine.
verses.263: Thus I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their guilt. I will put an end to the pride of the arrogant, the insolence of tyrants I will humble.
verses.264: I will make mortals more rare than pure gold, men, than gold of Ophir.
verses.265: For this I will make the heavens tremble and the earth shall be shaken from its place, At the wrath of the LORD of hosts on the day of his burning anger.
verses.266: Like a hunted gazelle, or a flock that no one gathers, Every man shall turn to his kindred and flee to his own land.
verses.267: Everyone who is caught shall be run through; to a man, they shall fall by the sword.
verses.268: Their infants shall be dashed to pieces in their sight; their houses shall be plundered and their wives ravished.
verses.269: I am stirring up against them the Medes, who think nothing of silver and take no delight in gold.
verses.270: The fruit of the womb they shall not spare, nor shall they have eyes of pity for children.
verses.271: And Babylon, the jewel of kingdoms, the glory and pride of the Chaldeans, Shall be overthrown by God like Sodom and like Gomorrah.
verses.272: She shall never be inhabited, nor dwelt in, from age to age; The Arab shall not pitch his tent there, nor shepherds couch their flocks.
verses.273: But wildcats shall rest there and owls shall fill the houses; There ostriches shall dwell, and satyrs shall dance.
verses.274: Desert beasts shall howl in her castles, and jackals in her luxurious palaces. Her time is near at hand and her days shall not be prolonged.
verses.307: Oracle on Moab: Laid waste in a night, Ar of Moab is destroyed; Laid waste in a night, Kir of Moab is destroyed.
verses.308: Up goes daughter Dibon to the high places to weep; Over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. Every head is shaved, every beard sheared off.
verses.309: In the streets they wear sackcloth, lamenting and weeping; On the rooftops and in the squares everyone wails.
verses.310: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out, they are heard as far as Jahaz. At this the loins of Moab tremble, his soul quivers within him;
verses.311: The heart of Moab cries out, his fugitives reach Zoar (Eglath-shelishiyah). The ascent of Luhith they climb weeping; On the way to Horonaim they utter rending cries.
verses.312: The waters of Nimrim have become a waste; The grass is withered, new growth is gone, nothing is green.
verses.313: So now whatever they have acquired or stored away they carry across the Gorge of the Poplars,
verses.314: For the cry has gone round the land of Moab; As far as Eglaim the wailing, and to Beer-elim, the wail.
verses.315: The waters of Dimon are filled with blood, but I will bring still more upon Dimon: Lions for those who are fleeing from Moab and for those who remain in the land!
verses.316: Send them forth, hugging the earth like reptiles, from Sela across the desert, to the mount of daughter Zion.
verses.317: Like flushed birds, like startled nestlings, Are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon.
verses.318: Offer counsel, take their part: at high noon let your shadow be like the night, To hide the outcasts, to conceal the fugitives.
verses.319: Let the outcasts of Moab live with you, be their shelter from the destroyer. When the struggle is ended, the ruin complete, and they have done with trampling the land,
verses.320: A throne shall be set up in mercy, and on it shall sit in fidelity (in David's tent) A judge upholding right and prompt to do justice.
verses.321: We have heard of the pride of Moab, how very proud he is, With his haughty, arrogant insolence that his empty words do not match.
verses.322: 4 Therefore Moab wails for Moab, everywhere they wail; For the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth they sigh, stricken with grief.
verses.323: The terraced slopes of Heshbon languish, the vines of Sibmah, Whose clusters overpowered the lords of nations, While they reached as far as Jazer and scattered over the desert, And whose branches spread forth and extended over the sea.
verses.324: Therefore I weep with Jazer for the vines of Sibmah; I water you with tears, Heshbon and Elealeh; For on your summer fruits and harvests the battle cry has fallen.
verses.325: From the orchards are taken away joy and gladness, In the vineyards there is no singing, no shout of joy; In the wine presses no one treads grapes, the vintage shout is stilled.
verses.326: Therefore for Moab my breast moans like a lyre, and my heart for Kir-hareseth.
verses.327: When Moab grows weary on the high places, he shall enter his sanctuary to pray, but it shall avail him nothing.
verses.328: This is the word the LORD spoke against Moab in times past.
verses.329: But now the LORD has spoken: In three years, like those of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be degraded despite all its great multitude; there shall be a remnant, very small and weak.
verses.330: Oracle on Damascus: Lo, Damascus shall cease to be a city and become a ruin;
verses.331: Her cities shall be forever abandoned, given over to flocks to lie in undisturbed.
verses.332: The fortress shall be lost to Ephraim and the kingdom to Damascus; The remnant of Aram shall have the same glory as the Israelites, says the LORD of hosts.
verses.333: On that day The glory of Jacob shall fade, and his full body grow thin,
verses.334: Like the reaper's mere armful of stalks when he gathers the standing grain; Or as when one gleans the ears in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.335: Only a scattering of grapes shall be left! As when an olive tree has been beaten, Two or three olives remain at the very top, four or five on its fruitful branches, says the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.336: On that day man shall look to his maker, his eyes turned toward the Holy One of Israel.
verses.337: He shall not look to the altars, his handiwork, nor shall he regard what his fingers have made: the sacred poles or the incense stands.
verses.338: On that day his strong cities shall be like those abandoned by the Hivites and Amorites When faced with the children of Israel: they shall be laid waste.
verses.339: For you have forgotten God, your savior, and remembered not the Rock, your strength. Therefore, though you plant your pagan plants and set out your foreign vine slips,
verses.340: Though you make them grow the day you plant them and make your sprouts blossom on the next morning, The harvest shall disappear on the day of the grievous blow, the incurable blight.
verses.341: Ah! the roaring of many peoples that roar like the roar of the seas! The surging of nations that surge like the surging of mighty waves!
verses.342: But God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far away; Windswept, like chaff on the mountains, like tumbleweed in a storm.
verses.343: In the evening, they spread terror, before morning, they are gone! Such is the portion of those who despoil us, the lot of those who plunder us.
verses.344: 2 Ah, land of buzzing insects, beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,
verses.345: Sending ambassadors by sea, in papyrus boats on the waters! Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and bronzed, To a people dreaded near and far, a nation strong and conquering, whose land is washed by rivers.
verses.346: All you who inhabit the world, who dwell on earth, When the signal is raised on the mountain, look! When the trumpet blows, listen!

verses.348: Before the vintage, when the flowering is ended, and the blooms are succeeded by ripening grapes, Then comes the cutting of branches with pruning hooks and the discarding of the lopped-off shoots.
verses.349: They shall all be left to the mountain birds of prey, and to the beasts in the land; The birds of prey shall summer on them and on them all the beasts of the earth shall winter.

verses.351: Oracle on Egypt: See, the LORD is riding on a swift cloud on his way to Egypt; The idols of Egypt tremble before him, the hearts of the Egyptians melt within them.
verses.352: I will rouse Egypt against Egypt: brother will war against brother, Neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kindgom.
verses.353: The courage of the Egyptians ebbs away within them, and I will bring to nought their counsel; They shall consult idols and charmers, ghosts and spirits.
verses.354: I will deliver Egypt into the power of a cruel master, A harsh king who shall rule over them, says the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
verses.355: The waters shall be drained from the sea, the river shall shrivel and dry up;
verses.356: Its streams shall become foul, and the canals of Egypt shall dwindle and dry up. Reeds and rushes shall wither away,
verses.357: and bulrushes on the bank of the Nile; All the sown land along the Nile shall dry up and blow away, and be no more.
verses.358: The fishermen shall mourn and lament, all who cast hook in the Nile; Those who spread their nets in the water shall pine away.
verses.359: The linen-workers shall be disappointed, the combers and weavers shall turn pale;
verses.360: The spinners shall be crushed, all the hired laborers shall be despondent.
verses.361: Utter fools are the princes of Zoan! the wisest of Pharaoh's advisers give stupid counsel. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a disciple of wise men, of ancient kings"?
verses.362: Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you and make known What the LORD of hosts has planned against Egypt.
verses.363: The princes of Zoan have become fools, the princes of Memphis have been deceived. The chiefs of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
verses.364: The LORD has prepared among them a spirit of dizziness, And they have made Egypt stagger in whatever she does, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.
verses.365: Egypt shall have no work to do for head or tail, palm branch or reed.
verses.366: On that day the Egyptians shall be like women, trembling with fear, because of the LORD of hosts shaking his fist at them.
verses.367: And the land of Judah shall be a terror to the Egyptians. Every time they remember Judah, they shall stand in dread because of the plan which the LORD of hosts has in mind for them.
verses.368: On that day there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt speaking the language of Canaan and swearing by the LORD of hosts; one shall be called "City of the Sun."
verses.369: On that day there shall be an altar to the LORD in the land of Egypt, and a sacred pillar to the LORD near the boundary.
verses.370: It shall be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt, when they cry out to the LORD against their oppressors, and he sends them a savior to defend and deliver them.
verses.371: The LORD shall make himself known to Egypt, and the Egyptians shall know the LORD in that day; they shall offer sacrifices and oblations, and fulfill the vows they make to the LORD.
verses.372: Although the LORD shall smite Egypt severely, he shall heal them; they shall turn to the LORD and he shall be won over and heal them.
verses.373: On that day there shall be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; the Assyrians shall enter Egypt, and the Egyptians enter Assyria, and Egypt shall serve Assyria.
verses.374: On that day Israel shall be a third party with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the land,
verses.375: when the LORD of hosts blesses it: "Blessed be my people Egypt, and the work of my hands Assyria, and my inheritance, Israel."

verses.377: the LORD gave a warning through Isaiah, the son of Amoz: Go and take off the sackcloth from your waist, and remove the sandals from your feet. This he did, walking naked and barefoot.

verses.379: so shall the king of Assyria lead away captives from Egypt, and exiles from Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, with buttocks uncovered (the shame of Egypt).
verses.380: They shall be dismayed and ashamed because of Ethiopia, their hope, and because of Egypt, their boast.
verses.381: The inhabitants of this coastland shall say on that day, "Look at our hope! We have fled here for help and deliverance from the king of Assyria; where can we flee now?"

verses.393: The watchman replies, "Morning has come, and again night. If you will ask, ask; come back again."

verses.395: Meet the thirsty, bring them water; you who dwell in the land of Tema, greet the fugitives with bread.
verses.396: They flee from the sword, from the whetted sword; From the taut bow, from the fury of battle.
verses.397: For thus says the Lord to me: In another year, like those of a hireling, all the glory of Kedar shall come to an end.
verses.398: Few of Kedar's stalwart archers shall remain, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
verses.399: Oracle of the Valley of Vision: What is the matter with you now, that you have gone up, all of you, to the housetops,
verses.400: O city full of noise and chaos, O wanton town! Your slain are not slain with the sword, nor killed in battle.
verses.401: All your leaders fled away together, fled afar off; All who were in you were captured together, captured without the use of a bow.
verses.402: At this I say: Turn away from me, let me weep bitterly; Do not try to comfort me for the ruin of the daughter of my people.

verses.404: Elam takes up the quivers, Aram mounts the horses, and Kir uncovers the shields.
verses.405: Your choice valleys are filled with chariots, and horses are posted at the gates,
verses.406: and shelter over Judah is removed. On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest;
verses.407: you saw that the breaches in the City of David were many; you collected the water of the lower pool.
verses.408: You numbered the houses of Jerusalem, tearing some down to strengthen the wall;
verses.409: you made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to the city's Maker, nor did you consider him who built it long ago.
verses.410: On that day the Lord, the GOD of hosts, called on you To weep and mourn, to shave your head and put on sackcloth.
verses.411: But look! you feast and celebrate, you slaughter oxen and butcher sheep, You eat meat and drink wine: "Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
verses.412: This reaches the ears of the LORD of hosts - You shall not be pardoned this wickedness till you die, says the Lord, the GOD of hosts.
verses.413: Thus says the Lord, the GOD of hosts: Up, go to that official, Shebna, master of the palace,
verses.414: Who has hewn for himself a sepulcher on a height and carved his tomb in the rock: "What are you doing here, and what people have you here, that here you have hewn for yourself a tomb?"
verses.415: The LORD shall hurl you down headlong, mortal man! He shall grip you firmly
verses.416: And roll you up and toss you like a ball into an open land To perish there, you and the chariots you glory in, you disgrace to your master's house!
verses.417: I will thrust you from your office and pull you down from your station.
verses.418: On that day I will summon my servant Eliakim, son of Hilkiah;
verses.419: I will clothe him with your robe, and gird him with your sash, and give over to him your authority. He shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.
verses.420: I will place the key of the House of David on his shoulder; when he opens, no one shall shut, when he shuts, no one shall open.
verses.421: I will fix him like a peg in a sure spot, to be a place of honor for his family;
verses.422: On him shall hang all the glory of his family: descendants and offspring, all the little dishes, from bowls to jugs.
verses.423: On that day, says the LORD of hosts, the peg fixed in a sure spot shall give way, break off and fall, and the weight that hung on it shall be done away with; for the LORD has spoken.
verses.424: Oracle on Tyre: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your port is destroyed; From the land of the Kittim 2 the news reaches them.
verses.425: Silence! you who dwell on the coast, you merchants of Sidon, Whose messengers crossed the sea
verses.426: over the deep waters. The grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue, and she the merchant among nations.
verses.427: Shame, O Sidon, fortress on the sea, for the sea has spoken: "I have not been in labor, nor given birth, nor raised young men, nor reared virgins."
verses.428: When it is heard in Egypt they shall be in anguish at the news of Tyre.
verses.429: Pass over to Tarshish, wailing, you who dwell on the coast!
verses.430: Is this your wanton city, whose origin is from old, Whose feet have taken her to dwell in distant lands?
verses.431: Who has planned such a thing against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, Whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the earth's honored men?
verses.432: The LORD of hosts has planned it, to disgrace all pride of majesty, to degrade all the earth's honored men.
verses.433: Cross to your own land, O ship of Tarshish; the harbor is no more.
verses.434: His hand he stretches out over the sea, he shakes kingdoms; The LORD has ordered the destruction of Canaan's strongholds.
verses.435: You shall exult no more, he says, you who are now oppressed, virgin daughter Sidon. Arise, pass over to the Kittim, even there you shall find no rest.
verses.436: (This people is the land of the Chaldeans, not Assyria.) She whom the impious founded, setting up towers for her, Has had her castles destroyed, and has been turned into a ruin.
verses.437: Lament, O ships of Tarshish, for your haven is destroyed.
verses.438: On that day, Tyre shall be forgotten for seventy years. With the days of another king, at the end of seventy years, it shall be for Tyre as in the song about the harlot:
verses.439: Take a harp, go about the city, O forgotten harlot; Pluck the strings skillfully, sing many songs, that they may remember you.
verses.440: At the end of the seventy years the LORD shall visit Tyre. She shall return to her hire and deal with all the world's kingdoms on the face of the earth.
verses.441: But her merchandise and her hire shall be sacred to the LORD. It shall not be stored up or laid away, but from her merchandise those who dwell before the LORD shall eat their fill and clothe themselves in choice attire.
verses.442: Lo, the LORD empties the land and lays it waste; he turns it upside down, scattering its inhabitants:
verses.443: Layman and priest alike, servant and master, The maid as her mistress, the buyer as the seller, The lender as the borrower, the creditor as the debtor.
verses.444: The earth is utterly laid waste, utterly stripped, for the LORD has decreed this thing.
verses.445: The earth mourns and fades, the world languishes and fades; both heaven and earth languish.
verses.446: The earth is polluted because of its inhabitants, who have transgressed laws, violated statutes, broken the ancient covenant.
verses.447: Therefore a curse devours the earth, and its inhabitants pay for their guilt; Therefore they who dwell on earth turn pale, and few men are left.
verses.448: The wine mourns, the vine languishes, all the merry-hearted groan.
verses.449: Stilled are the cheerful timbrels, ended the shouts of the jubilant, stilled is the cheerful harp.
verses.450: They cannot sing and drink wine; strong drink is bitter to those who partake of it.
verses.451: Broken down is the city of chaos, shut against entry, every house.
verses.452: In the streets they cry out for lack of wine; all joy has disappeared and cheer has left the land.
verses.453: In the city nothing remains but ruin; its gates are battered and desolate.
verses.454: Thus it is within the land, and among the peoples, As with an olive tree after it is beaten, as with a gleaning when the vintage is done.
verses.455: These lift up their voice in acclaim; from the sea they proclaim the majesty of the LORD:
verses.456: "For this, in the coastlands, give glory to the LORD! In the coastlands of the sea, to the name of the LORD, the God of Israel!"
verses.457: From the end of the earth we hear songs: "Splendor to the Just One!" But I said, "I am wasted, wasted away. Woe is me! The traitors betray: with treachery have the traitors betrayed!
verses.458: Terror, pit, and trap are upon you, inhabitant of the earth;
verses.459: He who flees at the sound of terror will fall into the pit; He who climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. For the windows on high will be opened and the foundations of the earth will shake.
verses.460: The earth will burst asunder, the earth will be shaken apart, the earth will be convulsed.
verses.461: The earth will reel like a drunkard, and it will sway like a hut; Its rebellion will weigh it down, until it falls, never to rise again."
verses.462: On that day the LORD will punish the host of the heavens in the heavens, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
verses.463: They will be gathered together like prisoners into a pit; They will be shut up in a dungeon, and after many days they will be punished.
verses.464: Then the moon will blush and the sun grow pale, For the LORD of hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, glorious in the sight of his elders.
verses.465: O LORD, you are my God, I will extol you and praise your name; For you have fulfilled your wonderful plans of old, faithful and true.
verses.466: For you have made the city a heap, the fortified city a ruin; The castle of the insolent is a city no more, nor ever to be rebuilt.
verses.467: Therefore a strong people will honor you, fierce nations will fear you.
verses.468: For you are a refuge to the poor, a refuge to the needy in distress; Shelter from the rain, shade from the heat. As with the cold rain,
verses.469: as with the desert heat, even so you quell the uproar of the wanton.
verses.470: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will provide for all peoples A feast of rich food and choice wines, juicy, rich food and pure, choice wines.
verses.471: On this mountain he will destroy the veil that veils all peoples, The web that is woven over all nations;
verses.472: he will destroy death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from all faces; The reproach of his people he will remove from the whole earth; for the LORD has spoken.
verses.473: On that day it will be said: "Behold our God, to whom we looked to save us! This is the LORD for whom we looked; let us rejoice and be glad that he has saved us!"
verses.474: For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain, but Moab will be trodden down as a straw is trodden down in the mire.
verses.475: He will stretch forth his hands in Moab as a swimmer extends his hands to swim; He will bring low their pride as his hands sweep over them.
verses.476: The high-walled fortress he will raze, and strike it down level with the earth, with the very dust.
verses.477: On that day they will sing this song in the land of Judah: "A strong city have we; he sets up walls and ramparts to protect us.
verses.478: Open up the gates to let in a nation that is just, one that keeps faith.
verses.479: A nation of firm purpose you keep in peace; in peace, for its trust in you."
verses.480: Trust in the LORD forever! For the LORD is an eternal Rock.
verses.481: He humbles those in high places, and the lofty city he brings down; He tumbles it to the ground, levels it with the dust.
verses.482: It is trampled underfoot by the needy, by the footsteps of the poor.
verses.483: The way of the just is smooth; the path of the just you make level.
verses.484: Yes, for your way and your judgments, O LORD, we look to you; Your name and your title are the desire of our souls.
verses.485: My soul yearns for you in the night, yes, my spirit within me keeps vigil for you; When your judgment dawns upon the earth, the world's inhabitants learn justice.
verses.486: The wicked man, spared, does not learn justice; in an upright land he acts perversely, and sees not the majesty of the LORD.
verses.487: O LORD, your hand is uplifted, but they behold it not; Let them be shamed when they see your zeal for your people: let the fire prepared for your enemies consume them.
verses.488: O LORD, you mete out peace to us, for it is you who have accomplished all we have done.
verses.489: O LORD, our God, other lords than you have ruled us; it is from you only that we can call upon your name.
verses.490: Dead they are, they have no life, shades that cannot rise; For you have punished and destroyed them, and wiped out all memory of them.
verses.491: You have increased the nation, O LORD, increased the nation to your own glory, and extended far all the borders of the land.
verses.492: O LORD, oppressed by your punishment, we cried out in anguish under your chastising.
verses.493: As a woman about to give birth writhes and cries out in her pains, so were we in your presence, O LORD.
verses.494: We conceived and writhed in pain, giving birth to wind; Salvation we have not achieved for the earth, the inhabitants of the world cannot bring it forth.
verses.495: But your dead shall live, their corpses shall rise; awake and sing, you who lie in the dust. For your dew is a dew of light, and the land of shades gives birth.
verses.496: Go, my people, enter your chambers, and close your doors behind you; Hide yourselves for a brief moment, until the wrath is past.
verses.497: See, the LORD goes forth from his place, to punish the wickedness of the earth's inhabitants; The earth will reveal the blood upon her, and no longer conceal her slain.
verses.511: Woe to the majestic garland of the drunkard Ephraim, To the fading blooms of his glorious beauty, on the head of him who is stupefied with wine.

verses.513: With feet that will trample the majestic garland of the drunkard Ephraim.
verses.514: The fading blooms of his glorious beauty on the head of the fertile valley Will be like an early fig before summer: when a man sees it, he picks and swallows it at once.

verses.519: "To whom would he impart knowledge? To whom would he convey the message? To those just weaned from milk, those taken from the breast?
